**Generated by:** Automation Design Architecture Agent (Stage 6)

## Section 0 — Framework Bootstrap Prerequisites (AA-1 only — first epic through the pipeline)

The repo is currently a bare Playwright/TypeScript scaffold (`playwright.config.ts`,
`tests/example.spec.ts`, no Cucumber). Every design below assumes these are in place before Stage 7
runs. This section will not repeat for AA-2 through AA-9 — it exists once, here.

**New `package.json` devDependencies needed:**
- `@cucumber/cucumber` — Gherkin runner
- `js-yaml` + `@types/js-yaml` — for `TestDataFactory` to read `test-data/*.yaml`
- `allure-cucumberjs` (or `allure-playwright` if Stage 7 opts for a hybrid runner — decide before
  first Stage 7 run, this document assumes `allure-cucumberjs`)
- `ts-node` — Cucumber's TypeScript step loading

**New config files needed:**
- `cucumber.mjs` (or `.cucumberrc`) at repo root — points at `features/**/*.feature` and
  `tests/step-definitions/**/*.steps.ts`, registers the `ToolshopWorld` custom World
- `support/world.ts` — the `ToolshopWorld` class (see Section 2)

This is infrastructure setup, not part of any single TC's effort estimate in
`automation_plan_AA-1.md` Section G — flag it as its own line item when Stage 7 first runs.

## Section 2 — Step Definition Architecture

### World interface (`support/world.ts`)

```typescript
import { setWorldConstructor, World, IWorldOptions } from '@cucumber/cucumber';
import { Browser, BrowserContext, Page } from '@playwright/test';
import { ToolshopUi } from './ToolshopUi';
import { ToolshopApi } from './ToolshopApi';

export interface ToolshopWorld extends World {
  browser: Browser;
  context: BrowserContext;
  page: Page;
  toolshopUi: ToolshopUi;
  toolshopApi: ToolshopApi;
  testData: Record<string, unknown>; // runtime data shared between steps (e.g. generated email)
}

export class ToolshopWorldImpl extends World implements ToolshopWorld {
  browser!: Browser;
  context!: BrowserContext;
  page!: Page;
  toolshopUi!: ToolshopUi;
  toolshopApi!: ToolshopApi;
  testData: Record<string, unknown> = {};

  constructor(options: IWorldOptions) {
    super(options);
  }
}

setWorldConstructor(ToolshopWorldImpl);
```

### Step definition table — `tests/step-definitions/aa-1/aa-10.steps.ts` (AA-10 — Register)

| Gherkin Step Text (exact) | Step Type | Method Name | ToolshopUi/ToolshopApi Call | Parameters |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "the user is not logged in" | Given | givenNotLoggedIn | (no-op — fresh context has no session) | none |
| "the user is on {string}" | Given | givenOnPage | toolshopUi.navigateTo(path) | path: string |
| "the user is on {string} with network capture enabled" | Given | givenOnPageWithCapture | toolshopUi.navigateTo(path); page.route/waitForResponse setup | path: string |
| "the user is on {string} with all other fields valid" | Given | givenOnPageWithValidDefaults | toolshopUi.navigateTo(path) + pre-fill via TestDataFactory.registerPersona() | path: string |
| "an account already exists for email {string}" | Given | givenAccountExists | toolshopApi.registerViaApi(TestDataFactory.registerPersona({email})) | email: string |
| "the user fills in the registration form with:" (data table) | When | whenFillsRegistrationForm | toolshopUi.register(fields) — fill only, no submit | fields: DataTable |
| "the user submits the registration form with a valid new persona" | When | whenSubmitsValidRegistration | toolshopUi.register(TestDataFactory.registerPersona()) | none |
| "the user submits the registration form again using the same email address" | When | whenResubmitsSameEmail | toolshopUi.register({...persona, email: this.testData.email}) | none |
| "the user leaves the {string} field empty" | When | whenLeavesFieldEmpty | toolshopUi.register({...validPersona, [field]: ''}) | field: string |
| "the user enters {string} in the Email address field" | When | whenEntersEmail | toolshopUi.updateFieldValue('email', value) | value: string |
| "the user enters {string} as the password" | When | whenEntersPassword | toolshopUi.updateFieldValue('password', value) | value: string |
| "the user clicks the {string} button" | When | whenClicksButton | toolshopUi.clickButton(label) | label: string |
| "the user is redirected to {string}" / "the {string} page" | Then | thenRedirectedTo | expect(page).toHaveURL(path) | path: string |
| "no error banner is shown" | Then | thenNoErrorBanner | expect(toolshopUi.getBannerLocator()).not.toBeVisible() | none |
| "{string} returns status {int}" | Then | thenApiReturnsStatus | expect(interceptedResponse.status()).toBe(status) | endpoint: string, status: number |
| "the app navigates to the {string} page" | Then | thenAppNavigatesTo | expect(page).toHaveURL(path) | path: string |
| "the page displays {string}" | Then | thenPageDisplays | expect(toolshopUi.getBannerMessage()).resolves.toBe(text) | text: string |
| "a field-level alert {string} is shown below the {string} field" | Then | thenFieldError | expect(toolshopUi.getFieldError(field)).resolves.toBe(message) | message: string, field: string |
| "{string} is not called" | Then | thenApiNotCalled | expect(networkLog.find(endpoint)).toBeUndefined() | endpoint: string |
| "the form does not submit" | Then | thenFormDoesNotSubmit | expect(page).toHaveURL(currentUrl) | none |
| "the {string} checklist item remains unmet" | Then | thenChecklistItemUnmet | expect(toolshopUi.isPasswordRuleMet(rule)).resolves.toBe(false) | rule: string |

### Step definition tables — AA-11 / AA-12 / AA-13 / AA-14 (representative subset; full set follows the
same pattern as AA-10 above — Stage 7 fills in the remainder per story using these conventions)

| Gherkin Step Text (exact) | Step Type | Method Name | ToolshopUi/ToolshopApi Call |
|---|---|---|---|
| "a registered account exists" | Given | givenRegisteredAccountExists | toolshopApi.registerViaApi(TestDataFactory.registerPersona()); store in this.testData |
| "the user logs in with the registered email and password" | When | whenLogsInWithRegistered | toolshopUi.login(this.testData.email, this.testData.password) |
| "the user submits valid login credentials" | When | whenSubmitsValidLogin | toolshopUi.login(email, password) with network capture |
| "the user is logged in" / "the user is logged in and on {string}" | Given | givenLoggedIn | toolshopApi.loginViaApi(...) → apply storageState → toolshopUi.navigateTo(path) |
| "the user has just logged in successfully" | Given | givenJustLoggedIn | toolshopUi.login(...) |
| "the user performs a hard page reload" | When | whenHardReload | page.reload({ waitUntil: 'load' }) |
| "the user inspects the top navigation" | When | whenInspectsNav | (no-op — assertion happens in Then) |
| "the {string} link is replaced by a {string} dropdown menu" | Then | thenNavShowsAccountMenu | expect(toolshopUi.getAccountMenuLabel()).resolves.toBe(name) |
| "the user opens the account dropdown" | When | whenOpensAccountMenu | toolshopUi.openAccountMenu() |
| "the user clicks {string}" | When | whenClicksNavItem | toolshopUi.clickNavItem(label) |
| "the user logs out" | When | whenLogsOut | toolshopUi.logout() |
| "the header reverts to showing the {string} link" | Then | thenHeaderShowsSignIn | expect(toolshopUi.getAccountMenuLabel()).resolves.toBeNull() |
| "the user is logged out" | Given | givenLoggedOut | (fresh unauthenticated context — no storageState applied) |
| "the user navigates directly to {string}" | When | whenNavigatesDirectlyTo | toolshopUi.navigateTo(path) |
| "the user is redirected to {string}" (post-logout, async) | Then | thenEventuallyRedirectedTo | expect(page).toHaveURL(path) — auto-retries, correctly waits out the ~1-2s async redirect confirmed live 2026-08-12 (see test_cases_AA-1.md Drift #4 — do NOT check page.url() immediately) |
| "the test observes network traffic for 5 seconds after logout completes" | When | whenObservesNetworkFor5s | await page.waitForTimeout is FORBIDDEN (Rule 6) — use page.waitForResponse with a timeout option instead, or poll network log for up to 5000ms via a bounded retry helper |
| "a login attempt has just failed with an incorrect password" | Given | givenFailedLoginAttempt | toolshopUi.login(email, 'WrongPass123!') expecting 401 |
| "the test checks session state via {string}" | When | whenChecksSessionViaApi | toolshopApi.getMe() |
| "the profile-fields form finishes loading" | When | whenProfileFormLoads | toolshopUi.waitForProfileFormReady() |
| "First name, Last name, ... are pre-filled ..." | Then | thenProfilePrefilled | expect(toolshopUi.getProfileFieldValues()).resolves.toMatchObject(persona) |
| "the user changes the Phone field to {string}" | When | whenChangesPhone | toolshopUi.updateProfile({ phone: value }) |
| "the user clicks the {string} button" (Update Profile) | When | whenClicksUpdateProfile | toolshopUi.clickButton('Update Profile') |
| "the new value is reflected immediately in the Phone field ..." | Then | thenPhoneReflected | expect(toolshopUi.getProfileFieldValues()).resolves.toMatchObject({phone: value}) |
| "the user clears the First name field" | When | whenClearsFirstName | toolshopUi.clearProfileField('firstName') |
| "the update is not saved" | Then | thenUpdateNotSaved | expect(toolshopUi.getProfileFieldValues()).resolves.toMatchObject(originalPersona) |

Note on RULE 6 (zero `waitForTimeout`) applied to `AA-1-TC-04-05`: the Gherkin step "observes network
traffic for 5 seconds" must NOT be implemented with `page.waitForTimeout(5000)`. Use
`page.waitForResponse(r => r.url().includes('/users/refresh'), { timeout: 5000 })` instead — this waits
for the actual event (or fails fast if it never fires) rather than blindly sleeping.

## Section 4 — ToolshopApi Class Additions

| Method | Signature | HTTP | Endpoint | Auth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `registerViaApi` | `async registerViaApi(payload: RegisterRequest): Promise<{status: number; body: RegisterSuccessResponse \| RegisterErrorResponse}>` | POST | `/users/register` | none |
| `loginViaApi` | `async loginViaApi(email: string, password: string): Promise<{status: number; body: LoginSuccessResponse \| LoginErrorResponse}>` | POST | `/users/login` | none |
| `getMe` | `async getMe(): Promise<{status: number; body?: MeResponse}>` | GET | `/users/me` | Bearer token from `this.token`, if set |

TypeScript interfaces for all three: see `support/types/AA-1.types.ts` (already written this stage) —
`RegisterRequest`/`RegisterSuccessResponse`/`RegisterErrorResponse`,
`LoginRequest`/`LoginSuccessResponse`/`LoginErrorResponse`, `MeResponse`.

**Not wrapped as a ToolshopApi method:** `GET /users/refresh` (AA-1-TC-04-05) — this scenario
specifically asserts on the *unsolicited* call the app itself fires post-logout, not a call the test
triggers. Intercept it via `page.waitForResponse()`, do not add a `refreshToken()` method that would
call it deliberately — that would test something different from what AC/Stage 4 actually verified.

## Section 5 — Fixture Additions

**FIXTURE:** `authenticatedPage`
- **TypeScript type:** `{ page: Page; user: { email: string; password: string; firstName: string; lastName: string } }`
- **Scope:** test (fresh persona per test — required per `test_plan_AA-1.md`'s shared-demo-store risk;
  do not reuse a persona across tests)
- **Depends on:** none
- **Setup:**
  ```typescript
  const persona = TestDataFactory.registerPersona();
  await toolshopApi.registerViaApi(persona);
  const { body: loginBody } = await toolshopApi.loginViaApi(persona.email, persona.password);
  const context = await browser.newContext({
    storageState: { origins: [{ origin: 'https://practicesoftwaretesting.com', localStorage: [
      { name: 'auth-token', value: loginBody.access_token }
    ]}] }
  });
  const page = await context.newPage();
  ```
- **Teardown:** `await context.close()`
- **Used by TC IDs:** AA-1-TC-02-03, 02-04, 04-01, 04-02, 04-03 (post-logout), 04-05, 05-01, 05-02, 05-04
- **Reason it's needed:** ~15 of the 25 scenarios require a pre-authenticated session; re-doing UI
  login in every scenario would be slow and duplicate what AA-1-TC-02-01/02-02 already test directly

### ✅ Storage mechanism resolved (was an open risk from Stage 1) — confirmed live 2026-08-11

Decoded a real login session directly: the token lives in **`localStorage`**, key **`auth-token`**, on
the **UI origin** (`https://practicesoftwaretesting.com` — not the API origin, since the Angular app
writes it client-side after login). No cookies are set at all. The fixture code above uses this
confirmed shape; the earlier `access_token`/API-origin guess in this section has been corrected.

### ⚠️ New, higher-priority risk uncovered while confirming the above — access tokens expire in 300 seconds

Decoding the JWT's `iat`/`exp` claims showed exactly a 5-minute lifetime — confirmed intentional by
calling `GET /users/refresh` directly with a valid token, which correctly returned `200` and a fresh
token with `"expires_in": 300`. This is **not** the same defect as `AA-1-TC-04-05` (that's specifically
the *unauthenticated* call returning 500 instead of 401) — this is a separate, framework-wide design
constraint:

- A **test-scoped** `authenticatedPage` fixture (fresh persona + login per test, as designed above) is
  safe — individual Playwright tests complete well within 5 minutes.
- A **worker-scoped or global** `storageState.json` generated once and reused across a whole suite run
  (a common Playwright optimization for speed) is **NOT safe** here — `test_plan_AA-1.md`'s own
  `@regression` target is < 15 minutes for AA-1 alone, and other epics' regression runs will also
  exceed 5 minutes. There is no working path to refresh an *already-expired* token (refresh only works
  on a still-valid one), so a suite-wide shared session would start failing partway through.
- **Recommendation for Stage 7 and beyond:** keep `authenticatedPage` test-scoped for every epic, not
  just AA-1 (this fixture is the dependency root all 9 epics consume per `requirements_AA-1.md`). Do
  not "optimize" it to worker-scoped later without re-solving the expiry problem (e.g. a periodic
  refresh call on an interval) — that optimization would silently reintroduce this failure mode.

### As-built amendment (Stage 7, 2026-08-12)

Stage 7's actual step definitions did NOT implement `authenticatedPage` as the `addInitScript`
token-injection fixture designed above. Most scenarios needing "an authenticated user" as a
precondition (AA-13, AA-14) instead drive a real UI login via `ToolshopUi.login()` — the same path
AA-11's scenarios use to specifically test the login UI itself. One authentication path used
everywhere was judged more valuable than the speed the token-injection shortcut would have added, so
`ToolshopWorld.loginAsFreshPersona()` was written, found unused, and removed rather than left as dead
code (see `support/world.ts`'s comment). The 300-second token-expiry risk and test-scoping guidance
above remain accurate regardless of mechanism — a real UI login still only takes a few seconds, well
inside the window.

## Section 7 — Cross-Layer Pattern For This Epic

AA-1 uses **two distinct cross-layer patterns** — Stage 7 must use the right one per scenario, not
default to one:

### Pattern A — intercept the network call a UI action triggers (registration/login confirmation)

Used by: AA-1-TC-01-02, AA-1-TC-02-02. The UI action IS the trigger; there is no separate API call to
make. This directly answers the "why send POST separately" question from earlier in this epic's
design discussion — there is no separate send, only an intercepted observation.

```gherkin
# From features/aa-1/aa-1.feature
@aa-11 @smoke @cross-layer @aa-1-tc-02-02
Scenario: AA-1-TC-02-02 — Login confirmed at the API layer
  Given a registered account exists
  And the user is on the "/auth/login" page with network capture enabled
  When the user submits valid login credentials
  Then "POST /users/login" returns status 200
  And "GET /users/me" returns status 200
```

```typescript
// tests/step-definitions/aa-1/aa-11.steps.ts
Given('the user is on {string} with network capture enabled',
  async function(this: ToolshopWorld, path: string) {
    // ARRANGE — start listening BEFORE the action that triggers the call
    this.testData.loginResponsePromise = this.page.waitForResponse(
      r => r.url().includes('/users/login')
    );
    await this.toolshopUi.navigateTo(path);
  }
);

When('the user submits valid login credentials',
  async function(this: ToolshopWorld) {
    // ACT — the click is the one and only action; it triggers the network call
    const { email, password } = this.testData.persona as { email: string; password: string };
    await this.toolshopUi.login(email, password);
  }
);

Then('{string} returns status {int}',
  async function(this: ToolshopWorld, endpoint: string, expectedStatus: number) {
    // ASSERT — observe the response that already happened, don't re-trigger it
    const response = await (this.testData.loginResponsePromise as Promise<Response>);
    expect(response.status()).toBe(expectedStatus);
  }
);
```

### Pattern B — direct API call for a follow-up assertion (session-state checks)

Used by: AA-1-TC-03-03, AA-1-TC-04-02, AA-1-TC-05-05. Here the UI action already completed in an
earlier step (a failed login, a logout); the follow-up check genuinely calls the API directly via
`ToolshopApi`, because there's no UI event to intercept — the point is confirming no session exists.

```gherkin
@aa-12 @regression @cross-layer @negative @aa-1-tc-03-03
Scenario: AA-1-TC-03-03 — No session/token created on failed login
  Given a login attempt has just failed with an incorrect password
  When the test checks session state via "GET /users/me"
  Then "GET /users/me" returns status 401
```

```typescript
// tests/step-definitions/aa-1/aa-12.steps.ts
When('the test checks session state via {string}',
  async function(this: ToolshopWorld, _endpoint: string) {
    // ACT — genuine direct API call, not an interception
    this.testData.meResult = await this.toolshopApi.getMe();
  }
);

Then('{string} returns status {int}',
  async function(this: ToolshopWorld, _endpoint: string, expectedStatus: number) {
    // ASSERT
    const result = this.testData.meResult as { status: number };
    expect(result.status).toBe(expectedStatus);
  }
);
```

| Password | `/auth/register`, `/auth/login` | data-test | `[data-test="password"]` | LOW | `register`, `login` |
| Register submit | `/auth/register` | data-test | `[data-test="register-submit"]` | LOW | `register` |
| Login submit | `/auth/login` | data-test | `[data-test="login-submit"]` | LOW | `login` |
| Update Profile submit | `/account/profile` | data-test | `[data-test="update-profile-submit"]` | LOW | `updateProfile` |
| Account dropdown trigger | header, all authenticated pages | data-test | `[data-test="nav-menu"]` | LOW | `openAccountMenu`, `getAccountMenuLabel` |
| My account (dropdown item) | header dropdown | data-test | `[data-test="nav-my-account"]` | LOW — confirmed live 2026-08-12; do NOT match by text/role, "My account" also appears as the `/account` page's own `<h1>` and causes a Playwright strict-mode violation | `clickNavItem` |
| My favorites (dropdown item) | header dropdown | data-test | `[data-test="nav-my-favorites"]` | LOW | `clickNavItem` |
| My profile (dropdown item) | header dropdown | data-test | `[data-test="nav-my-profile"]` | LOW | `clickNavItem` |
| My invoices (dropdown item) | header dropdown | data-test | `[data-test="nav-my-invoices"]` | LOW | `clickNavItem` |
| My messages (dropdown item) | header dropdown | data-test | `[data-test="nav-my-messages"]` | LOW | `clickNavItem` |
| Sign out link | header dropdown | data-test | `[data-test="nav-sign-out"]` | LOW | `logout`, `clickNavItem` |
| Field-level validation alert | `/auth/register`, `/auth/login` | data-test | `[data-test="{field-id}-error"]` (e.g. `first-name-error`, `email-error`) | LOW — confirmed live 2026-08-12, reliable `{field}-error` suffix pattern; can hold MULTIPLE concatenated validator messages at once (e.g. empty DOB shows both format + required text) — assert substring, not exact match | `getFieldError` |
| Top-of-form banner (register/login) | `/auth/register`, `/auth/login` | data-test | `[data-test="register-error"]` / `[data-test="login-error"]` | LOW — confirmed live 2026-08-12, reliable `{page}-error` pattern | `getBannerMessage` |
| Profile page banner (success + validation) | `/account/profile` | role | `getByRole('alert')` | LOW — confirmed live 2026-08-12: unlike register/login, this page's banners carry no `data-test`, but are reliably the page's sole `role="alert"` element | `getProfileBannerMessage` |

Rules applied (per Stage 6 template): `[data-test="..."]` preferred first (Toolshop's intended hook),
`getByRole()` used only where `data-test` wasn't confirmed during live verification — flagged MEDIUM
for a follow-up pass, not silently assumed. Zero XPath.
